speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Education in each year from 2017 to 2023 (a) how many international students who received the MOE Tuition Grant graduated from local Institutes of Higher Learning; (b) how many failed to update the Ministry of their employment status with Singapore entities within (i) one year (ii) two years or (iii) three years of graduation; and (c) what are the most common reasons cited for being unable to find work in Singapore entities.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Education in each year from 2017 to 2023 (a) how many international students who received the MOE Tuition Grant applied for bond deferments due to their inability to find work in a Singapore entity; and (b) how many were granted bond deferments on that basis.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can the Minister of State explained how exactly the Ministry pursues these students who do not fulfil their tuition grant obligations?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As I had explained earlier on, there is a serious view taken by the Ministry towards the obligations of these international students who have taken tuition grants.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: The Minister of State said actions will be taken to prevent them from working in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But is it not that one of the requirements of the tuition grants is for them to work in Singapore for three years after they graduate?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, is there any other measures that the Ministry takes to ensure that they pay back what they are supposed to pay back?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For the individuals who fail to honour their obligations for the tuition grants, we do look at the reasons.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Not that they do not want to find employment, but they want to pursue further studies.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For such cases, they will find employment after they have completed their further studies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Could I just check with the Minister of State two things?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: First, what is the breakeven in terms of taxpayers' subsidies for the number of years if one of these students were to stay in Singapore and work, in terms of, perhaps, what they return in tax revenues and the like, that would be taken from them when they work here.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For the first supplementary question, I do not have the answer off-hand.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I ask the Member to file another Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For the second one, having international students adds to the diversity of the overall education experience of our students and cultivates our students' sense of global orientation and ability to understand cultural practices across different nations.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think this is a healthy development and we want to encourage our students to be widely exposed to students of other nationalities.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask two supplementary questions to the Minister of State?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In fact, we do know of international students who previously were on tuition grant in Singapore having actually moved up and moved on to very successful careers within their countries and also regionally.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And certainly, this also augurs well for our economy because they stay connected, they understand Singapore's culture, and they do have friends and their networks built in Singapore while they were students here.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, there is definitely benefit in this regard and we will certainly be interested to find the information.
